meta.note: Built by tools/sanctuary/build_sanctuary.py from the research brief (Furtwängler 1906, text) and measurements/sanctuary-plan.json (Wikimedia plan, digitised). Verified text numbers win on numbers; the plan places and shapes; CONJECTURAL entries are labelled and provisional.
meta.displayLabel: c. 490 BC, Late Archaic sanctuary as completed

foundationDepth.note: DERIVED: west end of the terrace built up about 2.5-3 m (7 foundation courses, pp. 21-23); the skirt hides any gap to the terrain

rampWidth.note: plan measurement, +/-0.68 m; the text gives no width

temple.note: Ramp: slope 1:6 and 4.80 m long to the second step (pp. 25, 69) - with the provisional step rise the resolver's ramp is shorter (see dimensions.json).

terrain.note: Natural ground from the text (p. 21: steep fall east and north, gentler west and south; NE knoll at terrace height with a rock face to the cave; Südbau about 9 m below the stylobate, pp. 102-103); terrace surface at the base of the lowest step (pp. 69, 77). The scan covers only the temple (today's excavated ground) and is not used.

propylon.note: Matches the Ministry board: the only entrance, two columns between antae on each front, a central door, the approach rising from outside (south), a small sculpture on the roof. Floor at terrace height (orthostate cover slabs at terrace level, p. 77); the approach climbs to it over broad low ashlar terraces in front of the wall (terraces approach-tier-1..8; IMG_8191), which carry its southward projection, so no separate stair. The stair-side conflict with the plan is resolved by the board (sources.json choices.propylon-stairs-south).
